# pcd_identity_user_mfa (Resource)

Turns on multi-factor authentication (MFA) for a user, as the PCD UI's "Multifactor Authentication" user setting does: it enrolls a TOTP secret as a Keystone credential and sets the user's `multi_factor_auth_rules` to `[["password", "totp"]]`, so every login needs the password and a six-digit passcode from an authenticator app. Destroying the resource deletes its TOTP credential and, when the user has no other TOTP credential, removes the user's MFA rules, which lets the user log in with any method Keystone allows again.

Once MFA is on, Keystone checks the rules for every way the user logs in: the user can no longer authenticate with an application credential (for example one from `pcd_identity_application_credential`) or through single sign-on. Do not turn MFA on for a user that any provider configuration authenticates as, because the provider cannot supply a passcode. The provider refuses it only for the user of the provider configuration this resource uses.

The TOTP secret is stored in Terraform state (marked sensitive). Give it to the user's authenticator app as an `otpauth://totp/<issuer>:<user name>?secret=<totp_secret>&issuer=<issuer>` URI, the form the PCD UI shows as a QR code. Keystone accepts a passcode from any TOTP credential the user has, so a secret the user also enrolled in the PCD UI keeps working. While the user has another TOTP credential (the new one during a create-before-destroy replacement, or a secret the user enrolled themselves), destroying the resource deletes only its own credential, keeps the MFA rules and warns that the MFA rules were left in place. If nobody holds the secret of any remaining credential (for example the only one left was left behind by an interrupted create), the user cannot log in until the MFA rules are removed or a new secret is enrolled. To remove the rules when one TOTP credential remains, import it into this resource and destroy it, which removes the rules and the credential. To enroll a new secret, create this resource for the user again. Deleting a credential alone leaves the rules in place. To manage MFA a user already set up in the PCD UI, import it instead of creating it. Create replaces any MFA rules the user already had with `[["password", "totp"]]`, and a destroy that turns MFA off clears the rules rather than restoring the previous ones. Rename or move this resource with a `moved` block: destroying one instance while another is created for the same user in the same apply can leave MFA off until the next apply.

If the TOTP credential is deleted outside Terraform, the next refresh drops the resource and the next apply turns MFA on again; unless `totp_secret` is set, that enrolls a new secret, which the user must add to their authenticator app. Until that apply the MFA rules may still be in place, and a user with no other TOTP credential then cannot log in. To turn MFA off for such a user, apply first and then destroy: a destroy alone finds nothing to destroy and leaves the rules in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "alice_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "pcd_identity_user" "alice" {
  name     = "alice@example.com"
  password = var.alice_password
}

# Every login of alice now needs her password and a passcode from an
# authenticator app. The provider generates the secret.
resource "pcd_identity_user_mfa" "alice" {
  user_id = pcd_identity_user.alice.id
}

# The URI to enroll in the authenticator app, for example as a QR code.
output "alice_totp_uri" {
  value     = "otpauth://totp/PCD:${pcd_identity_user.alice.name}?secret=${pcd_identity_user_mfa.alice.totp_secret}&issuer=PCD"
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `user_id` (String) The user to turn MFA on for. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `region` (String) The region whose identity endpoint the provider uses; Keystone is global. Defaults to the provider's region. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `totp_secret` (String, Sensitive) The TOTP secret, base32 in upper case (`A`-`Z`, `2`-`7`) that decodes to whole bytes, at least 26 characters (128 bits, the least Keystone accepts). Omit it and the provider generates a 32-character secret (160 random bits). Either way it is stored in state. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `credential_id` (String) The ID of the Keystone credential that holds the TOTP secret.
- `enforced` (Boolean) Whether Keystone requires a TOTP passcode for every login of the user. Always `true` after an apply; a refresh reads `false` when the user's MFA rules were changed outside Terraform, and the next apply restores them.
- `id` (String) The user ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax. The IDs are assigned by PCD; the
[Importing guide](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/platform9/pcd/latest/docs/guides/importing)
explains how to look them up.

```shell
# The import ID is the user's ID (pcdctl user list); the provider finds the user's TOTP credential.
terraform import pcd_identity_user_mfa.example <user_id>
```
